title: Imaging and spectral sensing
text: **S01 · Biological observation candidate · Core imaging pathway**

pages.title: S01 Visible reflectance imaging
text: **S01 · Biological observation candidate · Core imaging pathway**

Visible reflectance imaging measures light returned from the plate, medium, disks and growth under a defined illumination geometry. A colour sensor samples spectral bands rather than measuring a complete reflectance spectrum. Exposure, illumination spectrum and image processing influence the recorded values alongside the object itself.
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is pixel intensity in digital counts. Calibrated spatial features can be expressed in millimetres, while colour or texture features require their own definitions. This pathway supports plate overview, disk localization, zone review and selected morphology research. Camera characterization can inform response and noise assessment. [R14]
## What the channel can support

The observation can support a reviewed geometrical measurement when the image and calibration are eligible. It cannot independently establish organism identity, a resistance mechanism or a quantitative MIC. Those outputs require a suitable assay or separately validated inference.

The proposed evaluation should compare measurements across plate positions, lighting drift and repeated loading. Preserve original images so that a reviewer can distinguish an algorithmic boundary error from a limitation in the acquired evidence. A failed reflectance image should remain a failed observation even if another mode later provides a usable view.
tables: Spatial target at the measurement plane; dark and uniform-field checks; colour reference when colour is analysed.
Glare, medium colour, condensation, automatic white balance, lid markings and uneven lawn appearance.
Stable optics and lighting, clean optical access, controlled focus and sufficient data storage.
Reliable contrast and spatial measurement across the intended plate domain, not maximum megapixel count.

pages.title: S02 Transmitted light imaging
text: **S02 · Biological observation candidate · Alternative optical geometry**

Transmitted-light imaging observes light that passes through the plate and its contents. Attenuation depends on absorption, scattering, thickness and optical path. It can provide contrast different from reflected light, particularly where the medium and vessel permit a useful transmission path.
## Signal and useful question

The camera records transmitted intensity in digital counts. A normalized transmission ratio is dimensionless when a suitable reference is available. The useful question is whether this geometry makes a relevant boundary or distribution more reproducible for the selected workflow. It should not be assumed to be interchangeable with the geometry specified by a standard reading method. [R03]
## Interpretation boundary

A darker region may reflect greater thickness or scattering rather than a proportional increase in biomass. Converting intensity into a biological quantity therefore requires an assay-specific calibration and a declared operating range.

A useful bench comparison would hold the object and camera geometry stable while examining how known optical disturbances affect the image. Subsequent plate evaluation should determine whether the transmitted view assists measurement or quality review. The software should retain mode identity so that a model cannot silently treat a transmitted image as a reflected one.
tables: Uniform backlight reference, dark response and spatial calibration through the complete vessel path.
Agar thickness, opaque media, bubbles, plate base curvature, labels and stray light.
Optical access below the plate, repeatable support and separation of direct from scattered light.
Measurable improvement in the intended feature without unacceptable position or medium dependence.

pages.title: S03 Oblique dark field imaging
text: **S03 · Biological observation candidate · Surface and scattering contrast**

Oblique and dark-field arrangements reduce direct light reaching the detector and emphasize light scattered by the object. They can make edges, texture and small surface features conspicuous. The resulting contrast is strongly dependent on illumination angle, collection geometry and the object’s scattering behaviour.
## Signal and useful question

The measured signal is spatial intensity in digital counts, often interpreted through normalized contrast or texture descriptors. Candidate questions include whether an unusual surface feature is present and whether a boundary remains visible when conventional illumination is ambiguous. Such images should be treated as complementary observations rather than automatically preferred measurements.
## Avoid a visibility trap

A bright feature in dark field is evidence of scattering, not proof of a colony or a resistant subpopulation. A scratch can be optically prominent while biologically irrelevant. The review workflow should retain the corresponding conventional image and the feature’s location.

Qualification should include objects that challenge specificity: clean vessel surfaces, known surface defects and representative permitted plates. If the mode changes the apparent zone boundary, the effect must be evaluated against the selected measurement definition. Its most appropriate initial role may be research annotation or artifact review rather than the sole source of a reported diameter.
tables: Fixed illumination geometry, repeatable reference texture and field uniformity assessment.
Scratches, dust, meniscus edges, lid defects, plate tilt and specular reflections.
Additional lighting positions, optical baffling and mode-specific acquisition control.
Incremental detectability with manageable false feature rates across vessel conditions.

pages.title: S04 Polarization resolved imaging
text: **S04 · Biological observation candidate · Polarization contrast**

Polarization-resolved imaging changes or measures the orientation state of light. Polarizers can suppress some specular reflections, while polarization-dependent signals may reveal optical structure. The benefit depends on the source, object, vessel and geometry; cross-polarization does not remove every reflection or scattering artifact.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include intensity at declared polarizer angles and dimensionless polarization contrast. More complete measurements can estimate polarization state under a calibrated instrument model. The near-term question is whether the approach improves readability or artifact discrimination for a specified plate and lid material.
## Preserve the comparison

The same region should be examined with and without the polarization arrangement so that a gain in readability can be distinguished from a change in appearance. A detector trained on one vessel material may learn its polarization artifacts and fail on another.

This candidate should begin as an optical quality improvement investigation. It is not a direct measurement of antimicrobial response. If selected, the configuration and angle state belong in the capture record, and any calibration affected by the added optics must be requalified. A nominally sharper image is insufficient evidence unless the intended measurement becomes more reliable.
tables: Polarizer orientation, extinction behaviour, illumination stability and channel registration.
Stress birefringence in plastics, depolarizing scattering, scratches, angle changes and reduced light throughput.
Additional optical elements, repeatable rotation or channel switching, exposure compensation.
Better usable-image coverage without biasing the feature being measured.

pages.title: S05 Near infrared imaging
text: **S05 · Biological observation candidate · Experimental spectral mode**

Near-infrared imaging uses wavelengths beyond the main visible band, with a compatible detector and optical path. Absorption and scattering can differ from visible-light behaviour, so a feature may gain or lose contrast. Those differences do not imply that near-infrared light will reliably see through condensation or every plate material.
## Signal and useful question

The recorded signal is wavelength-band-dependent image intensity. Spatial measurements remain in millimetres only after suitable calibration. The relevant research question is whether a defined near-infrared mode improves usable observation under particular media, lids or condensation conditions.
## Test the claim directly

The evaluation should preserve paired visible and near-infrared observations and independently assess the disturbance being addressed. Improved appearance in a few images is insufficient to establish a general “fog vision” capability. The comparison should include failure cases in which the added mode makes an edge less visible or creates misleading contrast.

Near-infrared imaging remains a proposed research pathway. It should not supply a biological ground truth or replace a missing standard observation automatically. The software should identify the spectral mode and require a separately qualified analysis route before using it for a reported measurement.
tables: Spectral response, source stability, dark response, focus and spatial calibration in the selected band.
Water absorption, vessel transmission, focus shift, detector sensitivity and differences in medium contrast.
Compatible illumination, optics and filtering; assessment of optical exposure and heating.
Verified improvement over visible controls across the declared disturbance range.

pages.title: S06 Ultraviolet excited autofluorescence
text: **S06 · Biological observation candidate · Fluorescence research**

Ultraviolet-excited autofluorescence observes light emitted after endogenous materials absorb excitation energy. The emitted signal can reflect several molecular and environmental contributions. The measured fluorescence is not a unique identifier of an organism or resistance state without an appropriately validated assay and analysis.
## Signal and useful question

The detector measures emission intensity within declared wavelength bands, usually in counts or normalized relative units unless radiometrically calibrated. Candidate questions concern whether a reproducible fluorescence contrast exists and whether it adds information beyond ordinary imaging in a defined research workflow.
## Treat the exposure as part of the experiment

Excitation can affect the specimen as well as reveal it. The research design should assess whether repeated observation changes the process being measured. The acquisition record should therefore retain exposure conditions and sequence history.

Initial use should focus on optical characterization and bounded research questions. Fluorescent reporters or added probes would constitute separate assay choices with their own validation and handling requirements. The product should not imply that a general fluorescence channel provides direct susceptibility, species identification or a clinically meaningful metabolic measurement merely because it produces a distinctive image.
tables: Excitation intensity, emission filters, detector response, background and reference fluorescence stability.
Medium fluorescence, vessel fluorescence, photobleaching, exposure history and spectral overlap.
Filtered optical paths, excitation containment, suitable materials and exposure assessment.
Reproducible signal separation with a credible control for non-biological background.

pages.title: S07 Fluorescence lifetime sensing
text: **S07 · Biological observation candidate · Time-resolved fluorescence research**

Fluorescence lifetime sensing measures the temporal decay of emission after excitation rather than relying only on brightness. A decay parameter can be influenced by the molecular environment and by mixtures of emitting species. The instrument response and analysis model are essential parts of the measurement. [R56]
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include photon arrival distributions, phase shifts or fitted decay times, commonly expressed in nanoseconds for relevant fluorophores. The proposed question is whether a stable time-resolved feature provides useful research information that intensity alone cannot supply.
## Do not overinterpret a fitted lifetime

A single fitted number can conceal a mixture of signals or an inadequate decay model. The research record should retain fitting assumptions, residuals and uncertainty. Comparisons across instruments require evidence that their timing responses and analysis methods produce comparable quantities.

This is an exploratory platform candidate, not a Reader V1 requirement. Its biological interpretation would need assay-specific studies and suitable controls. A technically successful lifetime measurement establishes that a temporal optical signal was measured; it does not establish that the signal identifies a pathogen, resistance mechanism or antimicrobial response. Selection should depend on a research question sufficiently important to justify the added optical and computational burden.
tables: Timing response, reference lifetime material, background and detector temporal behaviour.
Mixed emitters, low photon counts, scattering, photobleaching and model-dependent fitting.
Pulsed or modulated excitation, suitable detection, timing electronics and substantial analysis complexity.
Identifiable and reproducible decay parameters with an incremental benefit over simpler fluorescence measurements.

pages.title: S08 Multispectral imaging
text: **S08 · Biological observation candidate · Selected spectral bands**

Multispectral imaging records a limited set of spectral bands chosen for a particular measurement question. The bands may be acquired sequentially or through parallel optical paths. Unlike a colour photograph, the acquisition can be designed around specific spectral regions, but its usefulness still depends on the sample, illumination and detector response. [R55]
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is an image stack indexed by band, with calibrated or normalized intensity values. Ratios between bands are dimensionless but remain sensitive to how their signals were acquired. Candidate questions include whether spectral contrast improves artifact discrimination or characterizes a reproducible research phenotype.
## Select bands through evidence

Adding bands increases the number of possible correlations a model can learn. A band that appears predictive within one batch may encode lighting or medium differences. Selection should therefore be evaluated under site, batch and time separation, with a conventional baseline and an ablation analysis.

The resulting image stack is a richer observation, not a direct biological conclusion. The capture record should identify all band settings and mark incomplete stacks explicitly. If a required band fails, the system should use a separately evaluated reduced-band route or decline the inference rather than silently synthesize the missing measurement.
tables: Band transmission, source spectrum, flat-field response and spatial registration.
Motion between bands, exposure differences, spectral leakage, medium variation and detector drift.
Filters or multiple sources, synchronized switching, more data and a band-aware analysis pipeline.
Each retained band adds reproducible information on held-out observations.

pages.title: S09 Hyperspectral imaging
text: **S09 · Biological observation candidate · Spectral research**

Hyperspectral imaging samples a densely resolved spectral dimension together with spatial information. The result is a data cube whose coordinates describe position and wavelength. Acquisition may involve spatial or spectral scanning, so the cube may represent a sequence of observations rather than one instantaneous view. [R55]
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is intensity or calibrated reflectance as a function of wavelength and position. Spectral features can be described through band ratios, absorption features or learned representations. The research question is whether these features explain variation that a smaller set of selected bands cannot capture reliably.
## Control dimensionality and leakage

Many correlated spectral channels can make a small dataset appear highly separable. Model evaluation should therefore separate sites, batches and acquisition sessions, and feature selection must occur within the training process. A spectrum from one region should not be allowed to reveal the identity of the same plate in a test set.

Hyperspectral observation is an exploratory research option. A useful result could be a justified reduction to a few robust bands rather than a permanent requirement for a full spectral instrument. Biological interpretation and any susceptibility claim would need independent assay-specific evidence; a visually distinctive spectral map is not sufficient.
tables: Wavelength accuracy, spectral response, dark reference, spatial registration and illumination reference.
Spectral mixing, sample movement, stray light, medium composition and preprocessing choices.
Specialized optics, longer or more complex acquisition, large datasets and spectral quality control.
Reproducible incremental information relative to multispectral and ordinary imaging baselines.

pages.title: S10 Raman spectroscopy
text: **S10 · Biological observation candidate · Vibrational spectroscopy**

Raman spectroscopy measures inelastically scattered light whose frequency shift relates to molecular vibrational behaviour. Biological spectra can contain overlapping contributions from many constituents. The measured fingerprint depends on the optical system, sample state and background, as well as on biological composition.
## Signal and useful question

The output is intensity against Raman shift, conventionally expressed in inverse centimetres. Candidate research questions include whether spectra provide reproducible phenotypic information and whether an assay-specific response can be detected. Published work has investigated Raman observations with machine learning for microbial identification and susceptibility research; its results do not validate this proposed integration. [R44]
## Preserve what was actually measured

A spectrum taken from a selected microscopic region does not automatically represent the whole plate. The record should retain sampling location, selection method and any preparation required. A model should not report a measured gene merely because a spectral pattern correlates with a genotype in its training set.

This candidate belongs to a dedicated research track. The first decision is whether the intended question requires molecularly sensitive information and whether Raman provides it more usefully than a simpler method. Assay transfer, representative sampling and independent validation are likely to matter as much as spectral resolution.
tables: Wavenumber reference, spectral response, optical alignment and background characterization.
Fluorescence, substrate signal, medium residues, sample heterogeneity and laser-induced changes.
Spectrometer, stable excitation, optical containment, sensitive detection and often local sampling.
Reproducible biological information after controlling substrate and acquisition effects.
